statement: Every decoder phase cursor counter and terminal result remains in its declared domain
Every multibyte wire integer is fixed-width little-endian
No pointer-width or Rust representation detail affects canonical bytes
Magic schema version reserved flags and key codec identity must match exactly
Declared payload and complete frame lengths match exact bytes with no trailing input
Every length offset count and work calculation uses checked arithmetic
The complete byte limit is enforced before variable scanning hashing or allocation
Task dependency resource key profile event and receipt limits are admitted before allocation
Declared logical work is checked before variable decoding and cannot be exceeded
Cancellation is sampled before allocation at bounded scan intervals and before publication
Each retained output collection reserves at most once and only after complete admission
The exact 256-bit key codec identity is bound into every plan interpretation
Decoding then encoding every admitted key reproduces identical key bytes
Distinct caller keys cannot share one admitted encoded byte string
Plan bytes bind schema keys dependencies effects costs budget semantic profile and codec identity
Decoding an encoded plan reconstructs an exactly equal schedlib structural identity
Encoding any admitted decoded plan reproduces byte-identical canonical plan bytes
Every dependency endpoint names a task in the declared dense domain
Dependencies are lexicographically increasing and contain no duplicate
Every task read and write resource set is strictly increasing and duplicate free
The semantic profile is exact canonical UTF-8 and is never normalized implicitly
Plan and checkpoint digests use distinct immutable derive-key domains
A digest invocation binds format schema complete length and every frame byte
Digest mismatch returns no decoded object and performs no semantic publication
A checkpoint embeds a complete canonical plan that must equal the active structural plan
A matching finite plan digest never substitutes for exact structural plan equality
Checkpoint event count is at most task count plus one and receipt count is at most event count
Success events form exactly the initial canonical task prefix
At most one terminal event exists and it is the last event with a valid boundary
The zero-based resume cursor is derived uniquely from the success-prefix length
Published receipts are represented by one canonical prefix length no greater than events
Only the six declared event-kind discriminators are admitted
Checkpoint bytes contain no success failure or incomplete application payload
Checkpoint encode and decode preserve the exact plan event kinds receipt prefix and derived cursor
Resuming a decoded checkpoint produces the same canonical observation as uninterrupted schedlib execution
Re-encoding a decoded checkpoint before or after equivalent replay is byte identical
Native call-stack depth is constant in tasks dependencies resources events keys profiles and bytes
Encoding admission decoding hashing and reconstruction use linear work and retained heap
Concurrent invocations over immutable equal inputs produce byte-identical output and equal errors
Every malformed input returns one typed error without panic partial object or hidden side effect
